A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPH-RL research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original SQL and mathematical-reasoning experiments, including benchmark comparisons, divergence ablations, training curves, and solution-style analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds large-sampling-budget evaluation and data-partition ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same pre-sampling partition, exploration and preservation losses, and generator implementation. The divergence-definition implementation also matches across the appendices. The new threshold experiments vary existing settings rather than introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Coverage remains BIRD and Spider SQL, DAPO-17K-based mathematical training, and the same seven mathematical evaluation datasets. The multiple-style SQL scenario is retained. New sampling and partition experiments reuse existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The matched comparisons retain the same base models, GRPO, DAPO, RKL, and divergence variants. All four externally sourced SQL comparator rows remain in v2 Table 2/v3 Table 8. Experience-replay methods are newly discussed but not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation through k = 256 in Figure 2a and a Llama SQL partition sweep with a full-data control in Table 4. The 8-of-8 experiment retains all eight sampled trajectories per qualifying instance. These extend the experimental protocols; the original settings in Tables 6–7 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends analysis of two central questions: whether diversity advantages persist at large sampling budgets, and how the easy/hard partition affects performance. Figure 2a and Section 6.2 add sampling sensitivity and threshold/full-data controls absent from v2. Existing style, retention, and training-progress analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three separate Llama SQL training runs, display the same Figure 6 error bars, and select the model with the highest BIRD Pass@16. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark tables match numerically. New Table 4 reports BIRD greedy/Pass@16 of 61.4/73.5 under 8-of-8, versus 62.8/72.4 under the retained 6-of-8 setting. Figure 2a adds large-k curves, with DPH methods around 82% and the base model around 89% at k = 256. These are additional results under specified settings.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Theorem 1, the divergence definitions in Table 5, and the proof in v2 Appendix I/v3 Appendix J are unchanged. New Appendix D interprets existing likelihood and JS-mixture relationships through replay terminology without adding a formal guarantee or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and second contribution now explicitly distinguish improvements over GRPO from mitigation of Pass@k degradation relative to the base model. The conclusion newly recommends generator-based DPH-JS with an 8-of-8 threshold as optimal. The central diversity-preservation and forgetting claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 adds explanations of the greedy-accuracy/diversity tradeoff, selection bias, and possible memorization under the full-data setting. Appendix D explicitly interprets DPH-F as experience replay and DPH-JS as regularized rehearsal. The limitation concerning dependence on base-model capabilities is retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents the additional partition sizes and retention of all eight trajectories for the 8-of-8 experiment. Its abstract explicitly identifies the existing repository as providing code and data. The original hyperparameters, VeRL framework, hardware, and task prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix D add positioning relative to experience replay, citing Ouyang et al. and Zhang et al. (RLEP). Shen and Zhang is also added, while references to ZeroTuning, QwQ, Wenhao Deng's exploration work, and Guoqing Wang's information-gain work are removed. The distinction from offline preference optimization remains.

P1.justification: Related-work prose is condensed, Section 6 is reorganized, and training-progress discussion moves to the appendix. Appendix D adds explanatory prose, while most existing language remains intact. Author ordering, affiliations, equal-contribution information, and conference headers are also updated.

P2.justification: The visual organization is substantially revised: the style illustration, OmniSQL table, and training-progress figure move to the appendices. The former RKL plot becomes Figure 2b alongside a new large-k panel, the retention/exploration chart is redrawn as Figure 3, and a new partition-ablation Table 4 is added.

improvement.justification: The new partition controls and large-k evaluation address empirical gaps in v2, while the revised contribution better distinguishes beating GRPO from preserving base-model diversity. The gains are limited: Table 4 shows tradeoffs rather than a uniformly optimal 8-of-8 configuration, and that setting also changes trajectory retention. Appendix D's general dual-sampling explanation is not clearly reconciled with the retained generator implementation.
